newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Volvo unit says strike in Brazil over.
newsitem.headline: Volvo unit says strike in Brazil over.

text.p: Hundreds of workers at Volvo AB's Brazil unit returned to their jobs on Friday, ending a three-day strike over wages, a company spokesman said.

Volvo's chief spokesman in Brazil, Walter Viapiana, said striking workers at the firm's bus and truck plant in the Brazilian state of Parana decided to end the stoppage after a labour court judge ruled the strike was illegal.
The stoppage was ruled illegal because workers did not notify the company 48 hours in advance and did not follow strike rules laid down in Brazilian law, he said.
Company officials said between 300 and 700 of the company's 1,400 Brazilian employees walked off the job Tuesday.
Viapiana said the strike had set back output at Volvo's local unit by 45 heavy trucks and 21 buses but the firm was studying ways to recover production.
Brazil is Volvo's second and fourth largest market for buses and heavy trucks, respectively, he said.
